As of 31 July 2023 a cumulative value. REVIVE encourages and supports production of content addressing genderspecific topics such as sexual minorities womens empowerment and genderbased violence including harassment domestic violence human trafficking etc. which are not widely discussed or covered in the target countries. The content produced also portrays women in nonstereotypical ways and challenges gender biases. The projects emphasis on producing impactful content that challenges stereotypes and illuminates the roles and complexities faced by women and girls contributes to promoting gender equality and expanding the understanding of womens empowerment. Through capacitybuilding events REVIVE also collaborated with experts in gender studies and engaged them as speakers for instance at the Youth Content Creation Camps Activity 2.2. The project also ensures the active involvement of women as mentors trainers media experts producers or participants. To date the project has hired 23 women 45 to serve as mentors trainers and producers. Additionally a total of 154 women constituting 55 of the total number participants were actively engaged in the capacitybuilding events organised within the project.

Internews integrates gender considerations into its policies procedures and programming. The REVIVE project encouraged the production of content addressing genderspecific topics such as gender minorities womens empowerment and genderbased violence including harassment domestic violence and human trafficking which are not widely discussed or covered in the target countries. The supported content also portrayed women in nonstereotypical ways and challenged gender biases. The REVIVE team monitored the content production to ensure it reflected a genderbalanced perspective. Inclusion of female sources in the content was one of the assessment criteria of the content evaluation conducted within REVIVE. Project mentors supported the partners in covering gender issues including through expertise in development of scripts for the De Battle Talk Show on sexual minorities in KZ and mentoring for Zamira Baltayeva from UZ for her story on women and employment. Overall REVIVEs supported content challenged stereotypes and illuminated the challenges faced by women girls and gender minorities thus contributing to gender equality promotion. REVIVE also engaged gender experts for the Youth Content Creation Camps Activity 2.2. The project ensured active involvement of women as mentors trainers media experts producers and participants. 24 women 45 served as project mentors trainers and producers. 215 women 598 participated in the project capacitybuilding activities. By mainstreaming a crosscutting gender perspective Internews contributed to creating a more inclusive media landscape that promotes gender equality.

Extent to which the project activities contributed to promoting the empowerment of women and girls

As of 31 July 2023. By supporting the production of media content that challenges stereotypes and highlights the achievements of women in various fields the project contributes to reshaping societal perceptions. The pieces of content featuring women who have excelled in traditionally maledominated industries such as rescue service media literacy information technology law and geopolitics among others showcased their journeys challenges and successes and presented their opinions. These stories challenge stereotypes and promote equality and inspire young women to pursue careers without constraints. Moreover REVIVE emphasised the production of content on roles of women and girls as a part of Youth Content Creation Camps Activity 2.2 organised in Kazakhstan and Tajikistan. Out of 8 projects supported 4 focus on the topic. The programme of the Camps also included sessions on the roles of women and girls shedding light on existing stereotypes genderbiased language and the influence of traditions on perception of women and girls roles. Additionally best practices and case studies of content covering this topic were presented to the participants in both countries.

comment.narrative: Cumulative value

As of 31 July 2023 cumulative value. 47 41 coordination meetings and 6 joint actions. 31 coordination meetings with EU Delegations in the target countries were conducted on organising public events project progress and collaboration. 10 coordination meetings were conducted in Kyrgyzstan with multilateral institutions as UNDP UNESCO SOROS National Democratic Institute NDI to discuss the coordination of the media literacy initiatives. 6 joint actions with other institutions were implemented. Two capacitybuilding training sessions were organised in cooperation with the EU Delegation in Turkmenistan. Two events to commemorate the International Human Rights Day were organised in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. In Kazakhstan the event was organised in cooperation with the EU Delegation to Kazakhstan the Embassy of Netherlands in Kazakhstan and the Department of Media and Communication of KIMEP University. In Uzbekistan the event was organised in partnership with the EU Delegation to Uzbekistan the Embassy of the United States of America to Uzbekistan and the Public Foundation for Support and Development of National Mass Media. One presentation of results of the Rapid Assessment of media consumption was organised in Brussels Belgium in cooperation with the European Parliament and ENC. One presentation of the Tekshedrim information campaign hosting engaging activities on media and digital literacy was conducted in Bishkek Kyrgyzstan at the Europe Summer Festival organised by the EU Delegation to Kyrgyzstan.

Extent to which the project activities contributed to journalists of Central Asian countries to safely produce and distribute quality content and engage in crossborder collaborative projects

To a significant degree as evidenced by the following 1 the project subgrantees created 1682 pieces of informative content covering a wide range of topics. This highquality content broadened the audiences understanding of the current issues fostering a culture of informed and engaged citizenry as evidenced by audience viewership and engagement 2 the supported content produced within all activities reached over 66 million users garnering over 35 million views and more than 1.5 million engagements. This high reach and viewership helped create a more informed audience that was less susceptible to misinformation 3 all REVIVE partners saw growth in their subscriber numbers reaching a wider audience with factbased and engaging content while debunking false information. For example Khoma from TJ increased their social media subscriber base by an average of 40 while the Centre of Investigative Journalisms Telegram account in KZ doubled from 7.2K to 16.9K. PolitKlinikas account from KG also doubled from 37K to 77K and Botirjon Shermuhammads Migrant.uz channel from UZ saw a surge from 230K to 717K 212 of growth subscribers 4 by offering human interest and solutionoriented content the partners inspired individuals and organisations to make a difference and hold authorities to account. For instance a story by Alyona Aminova a stipend holder from Uzbekistan helped a family with a disability receive social housing while AsiaPlus content helped resolve a water supply issue in a remote area in Tajikistan 5 information campaigns in KZ KG TM TJ and UZ improved media literacy and critical thinking skills of audiences as suggested by audience engagement in activities 4479 participants content consumption over 95 million views and feedback from participants of media literacy campaigns. These activities received further support from the government authorities ensuring sustainability of media literacy work 6 thanks to Internews support 359 journalists content creators and activists along with 43 partner organisations were able to increase their awareness of propaganda tactics and develop proficiency in responsible and evidencebased reporting including about the war in Ukraine. This helped to foster a healthy information environment 7 Internews facilitated partnership building and crossborder collaboration among journalists content creators and civil activists within and beyond CA. This led to strengthening a network of independent media helping them to share experiences expertise and resources and promoted sustainability within the media industry 8 the support provided to the Media Action Platform in KG allowed it to evolve as an important and sustainable actor in civic processes and establish cooperation with other actors in the field. This work prevented the adoption of legal laws that could potentially restrict freedom of expression. This case also exemplifies the changes that resulted in collaborative efforts to build a more informed and resilient society.

Extent to which the project activities contributed to stabilisingnot worsening the situation in the Central Asian media and information space compared to the preimplementation period

The REVIVE project implementation period was marked by the tightening of control over independent media across CA countries particularly in Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan. However the REVIVE partners subgrantees continued to play a pivotal role in safeguarding press freedom and fostering a more resilient media landscape. The support provided by Internews contributed to the partners sustainability and capacitybuilding and strengthened networks and highquality content production. REVIVEs emergency digital and physical security support allowed to promptly react to the challenges faced by partners including criminal prosecution and digital vulnerabilities. Given the rapidly developing situation in the region and as per the agreement with the Contracting Authority this support was extended beyond project partners and included other independent media and content producers. Journalists from KG and TJ benefitted from psychological support to help them manage burnout and pressure. Internews collaborated with the Media Policy Institute MPI to provide legal support to partners like PolitKlinika Kloop.Media Media Hub 24. kg and the members of the Media Platform who faced pressure and prosecution for their work including for the content produced within REVIVE. The overall impact of the intervention contributed to stabilising the situation by supporting independent media outlets journalists and activists in the increasingly challenging environment.
